claims.text: TaVCrW is a disordered BCC refractory high-entropy alloy in the stated initial condition.

Replacing EAM and thermodynamic integration with an MTP and free-energy perturbation will accurately and efficiently determine melting and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of BCC refractory high-entropy alloys.
The proposed MTP can reproduce the ab initio phase-space distribution of multicomponent systems.
The MTP can attain training errors below 1 meV/atom.
Energy differences between the MTP and DFT have sufficiently small variance for efficient free-energy perturbation.
The small variance of MTP-to-DFT energy differences accelerates free-energy convergence.
A gap in the electronic density of states at the Fermi level produces electronic Gibbs-energy differences relevant to melting.
Solid-state short-range order stabilizes the alloy by approximately 2.4 meV/atom.
Electronic Gibbs-energy differences and solid-state short-range-order stabilization produce important shifts in melting temperature.
The proposed approach will save approximately 80% of computational resources relative to TOR-TILD.
The proposed approach will provide approximately a 20-fold speedup relative to TOR-TILD.
Free-energy differences obtained using FEP with an MTP and traditional TI with EAM will agree within 0.5 meV/atom.
Electronic excitations shift the predicted melting temperature by approximately 48–57 K.
The original TOR-TILD baseline uses two EAM potentials and ab initio molecular-dynamics-based thermodynamic integration.
The method is most applicable to high-entropy alloys resembling TaVCrW at high temperature under non-magnetic conditions.
The accuracy and applicability of the method are limited by the quality of the MTP training set.
Significant magnetic fluctuations may reduce the accuracy of the method.
Disagreement between GGA/LDA binding trends for V or Cr and CALPHAD data may limit accuracy.
Supercells of approximately 12×12×12, or about 3456 atoms, are suitable for MTP training and molecular dynamics.
Short-range-order effects are to be analyzed over approximately 2000–2400 K.

contradictions.description: An 80% resource saving corresponds to using 20% of the baseline resources, or roughly a 5-fold improvement, whereas a 20-fold speedup under comparable resource accounting corresponds to about a 95% saving. The two figures are presented as equivalent without explaining a different definition of resource use or speedup.
